title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document is the single-stop handbook reference for new and existing Redwood employees covering: working culture, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring & onboarding overview, and a guide to the primary internal tools. It is maintained by People Ops with contributions from Engineering, Product, and IT.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Intro
Redwood values engineering-first rigor, ownership, and empathy. We prioritize shipping reliable inference infrastructure, learning from production, and supporting each other to grow careers. The items below represent common expectations across teams.

Key principles
- Ownership: ship features and own runtime/operational quality until handover or retirement.
- Pragmatic iteration: favor shipping with measurable metrics and improving via post-deployment learnings.
- Respectful collaboration: asynchronous-first communication; be explicit about decisions and context.
- Customer focus: balance product velocity with reliability for customer-facing inference workloads.

Working patterns
- Core hours: teams generally align on a 10:00–16:00 PT overlap window for cross-functional collaboration.
- Meeting hygiene: agendas and decisions captured in meeting notes and linked to related Confluence pages.
- Oncall & rotations: teams with production responsibilities maintain oncall schedules documented in eng-sre/runbooks.

2) Roles & career ladders

Scope
This section summarizes typical role families and career ladders at Redwood. Each ladder includes the core expectations, typical years of experience, and promotion signals. Individual teams publish team-level ladders that map to these company-level bands.

Engineering ladder (IC focus) — represented levels
- E1 / Associate Engineer (IC1): Early-career engineers contributing to clearly scoped tasks; completes work with mentoring.
- E2 / Engineer (IC2): Independently delivers medium-scope tasks, contributes to code reviews, and owns small services.
- E3 / Senior Engineer (IC3): Designs subsystems, mentors juniors, drives medium-to-large features with cross-team impact.
- E4 / Staff Engineer (IC4): Technical leader across teams; owns architecture decisions, performance, and operational strategy.
- E5 / Principal Engineer (IC5): Company-level technical strategy, platform-wide improvements, and large cross-organizational initiatives.

Product ladder
- P1 / Associate PM: supports product discovery, writes PRDs for small features.
- P2 / PM: owns feature delivery and prioritization for defined product areas.
- P3 / Senior PM: owns multi-quarter roadmaps and coordinates across platform teams.
- P4 / Group PM / Director-level: leads product strategy for major product pillars (API, Dedicated, Private).

Managerial ladder
- First line managers: people managers who run 1:1s, performance reviews, and hiring for their squads.
- Senior managers / Directors: lead multiple squads, own hiring plans, budgets, and cross-functional programs.

Promotion signals (company-level examples)
- Delivery: consistent delivery of impact aligned to role expectations and measurable outcomes.
- Scope growth: taking on broader problems and reliably influencing cross-team outcomes.
- Mentorship and hiring: demonstrated mentorship and active participation in hiring pipeline.
- Technical excellence or product leadership: for ICs and PMs respectively, documented in performance reviews and portfolio work.

Promotion process overview
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: summary of work, impact metrics, peer feedback, and manager commentary.
2. Calibration: manager raises packet to the compensation & calibration committee with associated evidence.
3. Decision & feedback: outcome communicated with written feedback and a development plan if not approved.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & wellbeing
- Medical, dental, and vision plans for employees and dependents; flexible plans with HMO/PPO options.
- Mental health benefits include an EAP, therapy stipend, and monthly wellbeing allowance.

Compensation & equity
- Competitive base salaries with market reviews each year (comp cycles in November).
- Equity grants for all full-time employees with standard vesting schedule (4 years, 1-year cliff).
- Annual bonus program for eligible roles tied to company and individual performance metrics.

Time off & family
- Generous PTO policy (minimum 15 days + public holidays, adjusted by local law).
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary leave, 8 weeks secondary leave (local variations depending on region).
- Flexible work: standard remote-first policy with travel allowances for in-person meetups.

Learning & development
- Learning stipend (per year) for conferences, books, and courses.
- Manager-supported career development plans and mentorship programs.

Perks & office benefits
- Monthly home office stipend, commuter benefits where applicable, and catered team events for offices.
- Annual retreat and team offsites funded by the company.

Benefit administration and questions
- For benefits enrollment and plan details, contact hr@redwood.ai and refer to the benefits vendor portal (link available in the People Ops Confluence space).

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

High level hiring principles
- Candidate experience: timely communication, clear expectation setting, and transparent feedback.
- Interview consistency: structured rubrics and role-specific scorecards aligned with company competencies.
- Inclusive hiring: diverse interview panels and focused outreach to underrepresented groups.

Typical hiring workflow
1. Requisition & intake: hiring manager raises requisition with job spec and scorecard.
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiting conducts sourcing; initial screen with recruiter and hiring manager short screens.
3. Interview loop: technical interviews, system design or take-home (role dependent), cross-functional partner interviews, and culture fit.
4. Offer & negotiation: People Ops and hiring manager finalize offer; standard packages include equity, signing bonuses for select roles.
5. Preboarding: IT and People Ops provision accounts, equipment, and access before the start date.

Onboarding timeline (first 90 days)
- Day 0–7 (Preboarding): equipment delivered, accounts provisioned, welcome checklist and buddy assigned.
- Week 1: orientation session, security training, Slack/email introductions, and initial team onboarding plan.
- Month 1: complete role-specific training, shadowing, and first small deliverable.
- Month 2: ramp into independent work, regular feedback check-ins with manager and buddy.
- Month 3: performance checkpoint; written 90-day summary and career conversation.

New hire checklist (examples)
- Accounts: verified Okta SSO, Google workspace, Jira, Confluence, PagerDuty (if oncall), and GitHub.
- Security: complete security training & 2FA setup within 3 days.
- Compliance: sign NDAs and Code of Conduct.
- Tools access: request access to model catalog or Dedicated consoles as needed via internal tooling request form.

5) Internal tools guide (essential tools, owners, and quick tips)

Primary systems and owners
- Identity & Access (Okta + SCIM): owner: IT — contact it-support@redwood.ai.
- HR & payroll (Workday / Gusto): owner: People Ops — contact hr@redwood.ai.
- Code & CI (GitHub, GitHub Actions): owner: Eng Developer Experience — see eng-developer-experience/docs for repo naming conventions.
- Issue tracking (Jira): owner: Product Operations — use team-specific boards and the company-wide backlog for platform initiatives.
- Documentation (Confluence): owner: People Ops & Engineering Docs — structure by top-level spaces (see this page path).
- PagerDuty & Oncall rotations: owner: Eng SRE — rotation policies and runbooks in eng-sre/runbooks.
- Cloud console & billing: owner: Eng Infra — cloud-accounts-and-networking contains billing contacts.
- Model Catalog & Serving Console (Redwood Console internal): owner: Eng Platform — contact platform-ops@redwood.ai for provisioning.

How to request access
1. Open the IT access request form (internal link in People Ops space).
2. Select tool, provide justification, and list manager approval.
3. Track request status via the IT ticketing system; escalation to IT manager for urgent access.

Security & SSO notes
- All access requests require manager approval and justification.
- Sensitive environments (production model catalogs, customer data buckets) require RBAC approval and a business justification recorded in the request ticket.

Tooling best practices and conventions
- Repo naming: use team-prefix/service-name (e.g., serving-runtime-kernel).
- Branching & PR rules: small, self-contained PRs with descriptive titles and linked Jira ticket.
- Release cadence: document release notes and deploy runbooks in the release-notes directory before merging to main.

6) Ownership, escalation, and feedback

Document ownership
- This page is owned by People Ops (owner_team), with Engineering and Product as contributors. People Ops will review annually or when major policy changes occur.

Escalation paths
- Benefits & payroll issues: hr@redwood.ai.
- IT & access: it-support@redwood.ai.
- Security incidents: security@redwood.ai and follow the incident-response-security runbooks.
- Workplace concerns: contact your manager or people-ops-esc@redwood.ai for confidential support.

Providing feedback or suggesting updates
- Suggest edits via the Confluence comment thread or create a People Ops GitHub issue in the internal handbook repo.
- For changes that affect multiple teams (benefits, compensation cycles, or major process updates), People Ops will coordinate a review with reviewers and publish a changelog entry.

Appendix: quick reference tables

Promotion timeline & contacts
- Typical promotion review cadence: annual; ad-hoc promotions possible with sufficient evidence. Contact: people-ops-comp@redwood.ai.

Onboarding contact matrix
- People Ops: primary contact for offers, benefits, and policy — hr@redwood.ai.
- IT: equipment, access, SSO — it-support@redwood.ai.
- Manager: day-to-day onboarding plan and 90-day review.
- Buddy: peer-level day-to-day questions and team context.

Document maintenance log
- 2024-06-15: initial draft and company handbook consolidation.
- 2025-11-01: updated comp cycle and parental leave policy.
- 2026-03-04: clarified onboarding checklist and added model catalog access steps.

End of document
